messages:
sophie: Acme reporting p99 spikes ~30s starting 09:03 UTC. Customer sees intermittent 503s with 'request queued' in body. Opening triage here.

oncall-bot: Alert: latency_spike service=ingress p99=32.4s p95=8.9s. Incident INC-2026-321 created.

ben-sre: Quick look — ingress queue depth jumped. Pending requests ~750, active workers 180/200. Admission controller has been firing (rejecting at 80% util).

alex-eng: No deploys or config changes from our side since yesterday. Nothing in release notes.

maria-prod: Customer repro steps from their side:
1) curl -v https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" -d @payload.json
2) Several attempts return 503 and header X-Redwood-Queue: admitted=false
They can reproduce ~1/10 requests at peak.

kevin-ml: Model payload sizes normal (~4KB). No recent model swap for that tenant. Traffic pattern shows short burst from a batch job at 09:00 UTC.

ben-sre: Log snippet:
```
[09:03:12] ingress: enqueue request id=abcd1234 tenant=acme size=4280
[09:03:12] admission: pool=ingress util=0.82 admit=false reason=concurrency_limit
[09:03:13] worker: queue_len=762 active=181 pending=743
[09:03:13] response: status=503 tenant=acme msg="backpressure: please retry"
```

sophie: Is this a single-tenant burst? Can we temporarily exempt Acme or give them burst capacity?

ben-sre: Options:
- bump ingress pool replicas (fast, needs infra approval)
- raise admit threshold from 80% -> 90% (quick config flip)
- enable fallback routing to smaller model variant for that tenant
- ask customer to spread requests (but they need short-term fix)

alex-eng: I can push admit_threshold change: the flag is runtime-config/admit_threshold, safe to bump to 0.9 for 15m and revert. Will coordinate with infra.

maria-prod: If we can route Acme to smaller model for bursts that'd be best to preserve quality. They accept mild latency tradeoff.

ben-sre: Performing targeted mitigations now:
1) increase pool to 240 replicas via autoscaler API
2) set admit_threshold -> 0.9 for 10m
3) add tenant routing rule: acme -> model-compact as fallback

ben-sre: Command applied:
curl -X POST "https://infra.internal/api/autoscale" -H "Authorization: Bearer infra-token" -d '{"pool":"ingress","replicas":240}'

ben-sre: Runtime flag flipped: /admin/runtime set admit_threshold=0.9 (will auto-revert in 10m)

ben-sre: Tenant fallback rule added for acme: route to model-compact on admit=false

oncall-bot: Incident update: mitigations applied. Monitoring p99.

ben-sre: New metrics after actions: p99=1.1s p95=0.35s queue_pending=45 active=205

maria-prod: Customer confirms improvement, they're back to normal load. Thanks :tada:

alex-eng: Will follow up with longer-term fixes: smooth autoscaler ramp, refine admission policy to consider tenant priority, and add tenant-aware burst tokens.

sophie: Great. Please file follow-up runbook tasks and link here.

ben-sre: Created task: RB-3421 "ingress burst handling - tenant burst tokens" and attached notes from this thread.

sophie: Closing thread for now. Reopen if we see recurrence.
